paper.citation: Hedlund DP. Performance of Future Elite Players at the National Football League Scouting Combine. J Strength Cond Res. 2018;32(11):3112-3118.
paper.abstract: Secondary data from 2002 to 2016 for 5,506 NFL draft prospects and players linked NFL Scouting Combine measures (height, body mass, 40-yard dash, vertical jump, bench press, shuttle run and 3-cone drill) with draft and career data. Results are reported as position-specific means for players with no accolades, Pro Bowl selections and All-Pro selections.
paper.tldr: Combine measures differ by position and by Pro Bowl or All-Pro status, giving strength and conditioning staff descriptive position-specific reference profiles for American football athletes.
paper.methods: Retrospective analysis of publicly available data: combine results from CBSSports.com were manually merged with draft and career data from Pro-Football-Reference.com. The seven combine measures were averaged across eight position groups and three accolade categories, and the paper reports descriptive means, ranges and standard deviations without described inferential tests.
paper.findings: Means differed across positions and accolade groups, with the pattern varying by position. For example, quarterbacks with no accolades averaged a 4.83 s 40-yard dash, compared with 4.80 s for Pro Bowl and 4.77 s for All-Pro quarterbacks, and All-Pro quarterbacks were also taller and heavier on average than those with no accolades. The author notes that the profiles can help infer which position an athlete's test results might suit.
paper.limitations: The design is descriptive, with no inferential testing of group differences reported, and not all prospects completed every drill. Some players were still active, so career outcomes are incomplete, accolades are voting-based and imperfect markers of performance, and the abstract's description of running back body mass conflicts with the table and discussion.
paper.practicalImplications: Staff can compare an athlete's combine-type results with position-specific and accolade-group averages to frame training priorities. These are population averages rather than predictors of an individual's NFL career.
paper.athleteDev: The position-specific means for the seven combine measures provide reference profiles for strength and conditioning goal setting, such as the 40-yard dash and vertical jump values that separate accolade groups at each position. The data describe associations and do not show that training these measures causes career success.
paper.rtp: It does not inform return to sport: the study covers pre-draft combine results and NFL career accolades and does not address injury, rehabilitation or post-injury readiness. The values should not be used as return-to-play benchmarks.
